nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What were the two crop rotation systems used in the modeling?
nodes.answer: The two crop rotation systems used in the modeling were 500 hectares each, with one included in the LCA, dedicated to the cultivation of spring barley with under-sown cover crops (rotation 1).
nodes.paragraph: This was compared to the mono-digestion of cattle manure and a baseline sce- nario of soil incorporation of residues, using agricul- tural modelling and consequential LCA. We hypoth- esize that digesting cover crops and cattle manure would result in overall benefits for the environment, including ecosystems and resource availability due to displacement of natural gas. Methods Goal and scope Definition of the system An example-farm of 1,0 hectares and 560 dairy cat- tle was modelled, under Danish conditions. The num- ber of cattle was decided based on the amount of feed that could be produced at 1,0 hectares (detailed data included in the Supplementary information (SI)). The assessment was focused on the management of residues at the farm, including the cattle manure and the cover crop- and straw residues, applying conse- quential LCA methodology (Brand o et al. 2022). The farm area was divided into two crop rotation systems of 500 hectares each (rotation 1 and 2), of which one was included in the LCA (Fig. 1). These 500 hectares were used for cultivation of spring bar - ley, with under-sown cover crops (rotation 1).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Sustainable agriculture|Crop rotation systems_qna_001
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What types of cropping systems were evaluated in the study?
nodes.answer: The evaluated cropping systems included a low-diversified rotation of lentil-wheat-lentil-wheat, a moderately diversified rotation of pea-wheat-lentil-wheat, a highly diversified rotation of pea-mustard-lentil-wheat, and a wheat monocrop control.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Pulse crops are commonly used to improve nitrogen management and diversify cereal-based cropping systems. However, integrated assessments of diversified rotations with pulse crops using plant, soil, and environmental quality indicators remain limited and relatively underexplored. A comprehensive evaluation of such diversified rotations based on agronomic performance, economic returns, and environmental sustainability over time is essential for enhancing cropping system resilience. An eight-year study (two cycles of 4-year rotation) was conducted at two locations to determine the effects of diversification with pulses on ecosystem services indicators including productivity, resource use efficiency, soil carbon, soil nitrogen, carbon footprint, and economic returns. Four cropping systems were evaluated, including a low-diversified rota- tion of lentil-wheat-lentil-wheat, a moderately diversified rotation of pea-wheat-lentil-wheat, a highly diversified rotation of pea-mustard-lentil-wheat, and a wheat monocrop control. At the 4-year rotation level, diversified rotations increased yield by 22 36%, water use efficiency by 31 42%, energy productivity by 78 86%, and economic returns by 6 55%, compared to the wheat monocrop. Additionally, diversified rotations resulted in net CO2 withdrawal when accounting for carbon sequestra- tion in the soil.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Sustainable agriculture|Crop rotation systems_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How long did the crop rotation study last, and when was it conducted?
nodes.answer: The crop rotation study lasted 8 years and was conducted from 2010 to 2017.
nodes.paragraph: Wheat and pulse crops are dominant crops in the semi-arid Cana- dian prairie region, where Liu et al. (2020) reported effects of various pulse crops on productivity and soil organic car - bon in pulse-wheat cropping systems, but did not address Diversifying wheat -based cropping systems with pulse crops enhances ecosystem services 17 the impact of crop diversification with pulse crops on the overall performance of cropping systems. Further diversify - ing wheat-pulse cropping systems is considered a promising strategy to enhance the sustainability of cropping systems in this semi-arid region. The objective of this study was to assess the overall performance of cropping systems with different levels of diversification during an 8-year study period using multiple indicators collectively in the semi- arid Canadian prairies. We hypothesized that highly diversi- fied cropping systems would result in overall better system performance, as quantified by multiple ecosystem service indicators as shown in Fig. 1. 2 Materials and methods 2.1 Site description An 8-year crop rotation study was conducted from 2010 to 2017 on the research farm of Swift Current Research and Development Centre (50 16 N; 107 46 W; elevation: 825 m), Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, Swift Current, Sas- katchewan, Canada.
